kmap() has been deprecated in favor of kmap_local_page().
Therefore
column2: replace kmap() with kmap_local_page() in mm/memory.c.

column1: There are two main problems with kmap(): (1) It comes with an overhead as
the mapping space is restricted and protected by a global lock for
synchronization and (2) it also requires global TLB invalidation when the
kmap's pool wraps and it might block when the mapping space is fully
utilized until a slot becomes available.
With kmap_local_page() the mappings are per thread
page-faults
column2: and can be called from any context (including interrupts).

column1: It is faster than kmap() in kernels with HIGHMEM enabled.  The tasks can
be preempted and
column2: when they are scheduled to run again

column1: addresses are restored and still valid.
Obviously
column2: thread locality implies that the kernel virtual addresses

column1: returned by kmap_local_page() are only valid in the context of the callers
(i.e.
column2: they cannot be handed to other threads).

column1: The use of kmap_local_page() in mm/memory.c does not break the
above-mentioned assumption
column2: so it is allowed and preferred.
